page: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-128GB is a general-purpose cloud instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, offering 32 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with a single thread per core. Memory allocation is set at 128 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 500 GB of bundled local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier compute performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-10% results in single-core evaluation with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,669.0 and a multi-core score of 23,223.0. Raw processing throughput is further evidenced by a stress-ng single-core result of 3,883.99 and multi-core score of 100,920.97. Data handling is robust, highlighted by 41.32 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression and 365.09 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside memory read bandwidth reaching 235.89 GB/sec on large uncached blocks.

Without dedicated GPU accelerators, the instance is ill-suited for hardware-accelerated machine learning workloads, showing weak throughput on CPU-based LLM inference. In contrast, the system demonstrates strong efficiency across enterprise backend tasks, delivering top-25% results in Clang software compilation and PassMark database operations. The combination of high single-thread velocity, multi-core capacity, balanced memory density, and local SSD capacity makes this configuration well-matched for database servers, parallel CI/CD build environments, and enterprise application deployments.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-128GB is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM and driven by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. Featuring 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 128 GB of memory alongside 500 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Compute benchmarks place it in the top 10% for Geekbench single-core and multi-core workloads, supported by instruction support including AVX-512 and cryptographic offloading. While lacking GPU acceleration limits its utility for deep learning inference, memory bandwidth reaches 235.89 GB/sec for uncached blocks. This hardware allocation provides consistent throughput for database hosting, continuous integration pipelines, heavy compilation, and general enterprise workloads.
